title: Civil Engineering Salary in Australia: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to calculate a civil engineering salary in Australia using hourly rates, award minimums, and market data. Includes tax, super, and fortnightly pay estimates.
salarySummary: For a civil engineer earning the median hourly rate of $59, working 38 hours per week, the annual gross salary is approximately $116,584 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a civil engineer under the Professional Employees Award?
faqs.a: Under the Professional Employees Award 2020, a Level 1 graduate professional (3-year degree) has a minimum hourly rate of $33.71, while a Level 2 experienced professional earns $39.77 per hour. These rates apply from 1 July 2026 and are the legal minimums for award-covered employees. Higher rates may apply under enterprise agreements or market conditions.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for civil engineers?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026) up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, on an annual salary of $116,584, the super contribution would be about $13,990. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit paid into your super fund.

faqs.q: What is the difference between award rates and median market rates for civil engineers?
faqs.a: Award rates are the legal minimums set by the Fair Work Commission. For civil engineers, the median market hourly rate is $59 per hour (from ABS data), which is significantly higher than the award Level 2 rate of $39.77. The median full-time weekly earnings are $2,217, reflecting experience, qualifications, and market demand. Award rates apply to those covered by the award, but many engineers earn above award.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Civil Engineering Salary in Australia

When researching a **civil engineering salary in Australia**, it helps to start with the hourly rate and work up to annual, fortnightly, and after-tax figures. This guide uses the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Professional Employees Award 2020, the Australian Bureau of Statistics’ earnings data, and the 2026–27 tax rates to give you a clear picture.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The standard calculation is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee under the award, ordinary hours are 38 per week (). If your actual hours differ, adjust accordingly. The same formula works for part-time and casual employees, but casuals receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate.

### Award Minimums for Civil Engineers

The Professional Employees Award 2020 covers many civil engineering roles. From 1 July 2026, the minimum annual wages and hourly rates are:

- Level 1 Graduate (3-year degree): $66,825 per year / $33.71 per hour
- Level 1 Graduate (4 or 5-year degree): $68,538 / $34.57
- Level 2 Experienced professional: $78,836 / $39.77
- Level 3 Professional/Senior: $86,157 / $43.46
- Level 4 Professional: $97,173 / $49.02
- Level 5 Experienced medical research (not typical for civil): $117,064 / $59.05

These rates are the legal minimums. Most civil engineers with experience earn above these levels. The award also provides penalty rates for work outside ordinary hours, overtime, and casual loading ().

### Market Median: What Civil Engineers Actually Earn

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (via Jobs and Skills Australia), the median hourly earnings for full-time non-managerial civil engineering professionals is **$59 per hour**, and median weekly earnings are **$2,217** (). This is based on a 44-hour average week, but for consistency with award calculations, we use 38 hours to estimate annual pay.

Using the median hourly rate of $59:

- Annual gross (38 hours): $59 × 38 × 52 = **$116,584**
- Fortnightly gross: $116,584 ÷ 26 = **$4,484**

This is well above the award minimums and reflects the market value for experienced engineers.

### Tax and Medicare on Your Civil Engineering Salary

For the 2026–27 income year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% for each dollar over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% for each dollar over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% for each dollar over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% for each dollar over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed).

Example tax estimate on $116,584:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201–$45,000: 15% of $26,800 = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001–$116,584: 30% of $71,584 = $21,475.20
- Total tax: $25,495.20
- Medicare levy (2%): $2,331.68
- Total tax + Medicare: $27,826.88
- After-tax annual: $88,757.12
- After-tax fortnightly: $3,413.73

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool to personalise your figures.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For the $116,584 example, that’s an extra $13,990 per year contributed to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is not deducted from your pay. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Casual Loading and Part-Time Work

If you work as a casual civil engineer, you are entitled to a 25% loading on the base hourly rate instead of paid leave. For example, on the award Level 2 rate of $39.77, the casual rate is $39.77 × 1.25 = $49.71 per hour. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how this affects annual estimates.

Part-time employees are paid pro-rata on the same hourly rates as full-timers, working fewer than 38 hours per week by agreement.

### Important Notes on This Estimate

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a quick conversion of any hourly rate, use [the timesheet](/) to see annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures with tax and super included.
